headline: Build the cheapest composition for each amount
statement: Given distinct positive coin denominations and an amount, return the fewest coins whose values sum to amount. Every denomination may be used any number of times. Return -1 when the amount cannot be formed.
intuition: For each amount, ask which coin could be the last one used. Removing that coin leaves a smaller amount whose best answer is already saved. Add one coin to that answer and choose the smallest count. This avoids repeatedly solving the same smaller amounts.
approach: Set dp[0]=0 and every other entry to an unreachable sentinel.
For each amount from 1 upward, try every coin not exceeding it.
Convert an unreachable final value to -1.
correctness: Any nonempty coin composition has a final coin c and a composition of value-c. Inductively dp[value-c] is its best possible cost. Trying every c therefore considers a best possible composition’s last coin, and no candidate can be cheaper than a real composition. The minimum is exact.
bruteForce: Recursively try every possible next coin without storing repeated amounts; the branching causes exponential repeated work.

complexity.explanation: Each table entry examines all denominations; amount+1 slots hold best possible counts.

pitfalls: Largest-coin-first is not valid for arbitrary denominations.
Use a sentinel greater than any possible valid coin count.
